sections.kicker: Prepared for Teevolution by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Teevolution wants to feel fresh. Its front door still talks like a spec sheet.
sections.keep: The reviewers on your site, from Randomfrankp to Horcus. Real people with real audiences, already on your side.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.quote: This is a G703 super light.
pins.what: The loudest proof on the site defines Teevolution as another brand's alternative.
pins.why: Borrowed identity and model numbers are exactly the serious, technical feel you want to leave.
pins.how: Keep the reviewers, but put your own idea in front of them.
pins.label: Your reviews
pins.cost: Players remember the mouse you copy, not the brand you are.

pins.quote: The gear that evolves with you.
pins.what: The tagline could sit on any peripheral box.
pins.why: It talks about the product, not the culture you want to be part of.
pins.how: Say something only a player would recognise.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: Followers get no reason to wear the brand, only to buy the mouse.

pins.what: The section heading frames gear as a lab test.
pins.why: Experts make it serious; players make it culture.
pins.how: Let players, setups and stories carry the voice.
pins.label: Your site
pins.cost: The brand stays a reviewer's pick instead of a crowd.

sections.intro: You said you want gaming gear that does not feel too serious and technical. Here is where the site and the bio pull the other way.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on Teevolution's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
